correctness.rationale: For exact Wang–Zhong ellipse-map coefficients a=-10/11,b=1/44; A,B negative and C,D positive, with |A|>27/25. The binomial theorem gives p_m’=1+sum_j binom(m,j) A^j B^(m-j) S_{a^j b^(m-j)} and q_m’=sum_j binom(m,j) D^j C^(m-j) S_{...}, S_t(x)=x(2-tx)/(1-tx)^2. For any nonzero real x in [-1,1], all S_t(x) have sign x, so q_m’(x) is nonzero with sign x. At epsilon_m=(-1)^(m+1), all analytic derivative tail summands are negative; j=m gives p_m’(epsilon_m)<=1-|A|^m F((10/11)^m), F(u)=(2+u)/(1+u)^2 decreases with u. For m>=3 the latter product exceeds its m=3 lower bound (27/25)^3 F((10/11)^3)=1+136271021/1048140625. Thus p_m’(epsilon_m)<0, p_m’(0)=1 and intermediate value yields an interior signed root where J=-|q_m’|²<0. Since J(0)=1, Lewy local univalence necessity excludes local univalence on the disk. Independently calculated exact rational boundary bounds and located signed zeros for sample m=3..10; universal proof is monotonicity, not those finite tests. The m=2 nonunivalence is explicitly credited to original 2026 source.
